processing: Mainly steamed and rolled as sencha. Withering brings out a floral scent, and it also suits oolong-style processing.
harvest_season: Early spring, about 3 to 5 days before Yabukita.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf pieces, as with other steamed greens.
taste_profile: Sweet and floral in the aroma, with a fresh green sencha body; more perfumed if the leaf was withered.

brewing.notes: Usual sencha settings; slightly hotter water brings out the aroma. Oolong-style lots can take water near 90°C.

vintage_note: As with Japanese sencha generally, it is sold from the current year's harvest and is best drunk fresh. It appears mostly as small single-cultivar lots, which name the grower and year, and sometimes as withered or semi-oxidised tea.
description:
Yumekaori is a newer cultivar from Miyazaki in southern Japan, and its name means dream aroma. It was bred above all as a farming solution: it was the first Japanese cultivar selected for resistance to white peach scale, a common tea pest.

Its name still suits the cup. When withered the leaf gives a pleasant floral smell, and it makes good sencha with dark, lustrous leaves. It also works as oolong.

Expect a sweet floral aroma on top of a typical sencha body. Start with ordinary sencha settings, then try a little hotter to bring up the fragrance.

It is a small-lot tea. Check whether the leaf was withered, since that changes the character a lot. It is weak against anthracnose and bacterial shoot blight, so it stays a careful grower's plant.
history: Yumekaori was bred at the tea branch of Miyazaki Prefecture's agricultural research institute. The cross of Sayamakaori and Miyazaki No. 8 was made in 1986, and the cultivar was registered in 2006.
